correctness.rationale: The open-neighborhood bit-union predicate exactly encodes total domination on all 20 vertices; two standalone programs exhaust all subsets through size eight and prove no smaller set works. They independently reconstruct the full 190-state jump and slide graphs. Every connected-component eccentricity is computed; 20 six-cycles and the thirty 4+4 hub-incidences are exhaustively checked. An exact 20-element vertex bijection compares all 30 quotient edges with GP(10,3), and a separate verifier finds an isomorphism without loading that map. Two explicit edge-preserving generators yield 120 automorphisms, matching a separate exhaustive adjacency-preserving permutation backtracking enumeration, and prove all five orbits.

value.rationale: The nontrivial theorem identifies an exact Desargues graph as the intrinsic incidence quotient of twenty disjoint hexagons and thirty hubs in a distinct dodecahedral optimal-monitoring space, with explicit certified bijection. It also gives a sharp and substantial movement obstruction (190 frozen slides, 40 frozen jumps, one self-centered 150-state component of eccentricity ten), and a five-orbit classification. This is a natural structural classification of mobility and graph-to-graph relation, not merely a small count or routine specialization.
